title: Measurement-Only Dynamical Phase Transitions in Spin-1 Chains
authors: Kemal Aziz, Haining Pan, J. H. Pixley
abstract: We study measurement-only dynamics in an interacting spin-1 chain, using forced, normalized local projections rather than Born-rule-sampled measurement outcomes. Starting from the nearest-neighbor (NN) Affleck-Kennedy-Lieb-Tasaki (AKLT) Haldane symmetry-protected topological state, we show that competing local projectors drive this order toward three distinct dynamical phases: a featureless topologically trivial product state, an explicitly dimerized valence-bond-solid state, and a topologically trivial next-nearest-neighbor (NNN) AKLT state consisting of two interwoven Haldane chains. Using matrix product state and exact statevector simulations, we identify continuous transitions among these phases and characterize them using nonlocal string order parameters, local dimer order, and entanglement scaling. For the NN-NNN AKLT model, finite-size signatures are consistent with an intervening extended critical regime rather than a single direct transition. These results extend studies of monitored topology to a bosonic SPT and show that local projections can control both topological and valence-bond-solid order.
summary: This paper explores how measurement-only dynamics can induce phase transitions in an interacting spin-1 chain, moving beyond standard unitary evolution. By competing local projectors, the system is shown to transition between topologically distinct phases, characterized by measurable order parameters and entanglement scaling. It provides a powerful tool for studying non-equilibrium quantum matter.
main_problem: The study investigates dynamical phase transitions occurring in an interacting spin-1 chain driven solely by sequential, forced local measurements rather than standard unitary evolution.
main_result: Competing local projectors can drive the system through three distinct dynamical phases—a trivial product state, a dimerized VBS state, and an NNN AKLT state—with evidence suggesting intervening extended critical regimes.
method: The analysis employs matrix product state (MPS) simulations and exact statevector calculations to track the evolution under forced local projections, supplemented by finite-size scaling analysis.
model_or_system: The system is a spin-1 chain, starting from the nearest-neighbor (NN) Affleck-Kennedy-Lieb-Tasaki (AKLT) Haldane symmetry-protected topological (SPT) state. The dynamics are governed by the competition between projectors corresponding to NN AKLT, Dimer VBS, and NNN AKLT interactions.
key_observables: Nonlocal string order parameters, local dimer order, entanglement scaling, and the MPS bond dimension ($\chi$).
important_parameters: The relative strengths/probabilities of the competing local projectors (e.g., $p_{	ext{nnn},c} \simeq 0.28$ and $p_{	ext{nnn},c} \simeq 0.64$).
main_assumptions: The dynamics are modeled using forced, normalized local projections, which bypass the constraints of unitary evolution, and the analysis relies on specific transfer-matrix identities for observables.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the three competing projector protocols (NN AKLT, Dimer, NNN AKLT) and show objective landscapes for statevector collapses and the time evolution of entanglement entropy in different phases.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the effect of competing local projectors on the spin-1 chain, characterizing the resulting dynamical phases using multiple order parameters and performing finite-size scaling to locate critical points.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, measurable framework for understanding how non-unitary, measurement-induced dynamics can stabilize or transition between distinct topological and valence-bond-solid orders in quantum magnets.
